title: Weights of KZ motives and quantum groups
summary:
The Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov (KZ) connection is defined on the constant bundle determined by $n$ finite-dimensional irreducible representations of a simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ and a nonzero complex parameter $κ$, over the configuration space of $n$ distinct points on the affine line. Work of Schechtman--Varchenko and Looijenga shows that, when $κ$ is rational, the resulting local systems admit natural motivic realizations, called KZ motives.
  The Kazhdan--Lusztig equivalence identifies the local systems underlying these motivic variations with certain representations of the pure braid group arising from the corresponding Lusztig quantum group at a root of unity. We formulate conjectures relating the weight filtrations of KZ motives to structures in quantum-group representation theory, particularly tilting modules and the Jantzen and Andersen filtrations, and provide evidence for these conjectures.
  Our methods use a new deformation of the representation ring that records the first moments of the weight filtration, together with Schmid's theorem on limiting mixed Hodge structures and results on the Hodge filtration obtained in earlier joint work with S. Mukhopadhyay.

title: Large-Level Limit of Doubled Chern-Simons Theory Part I: Regular Sector, Boundaries and Interfaces
summary: We study three-dimensional $BF$ theory as the large-level limit of the doubled Chern--Simons theory $G_k\times G_{-k}$ for simply connected, compact, simple $G$, a limit that connects the symmetry topological field theories of finite and continuous symmetries. Lines whose two highest weights grow linearly with $k$ at fixed difference become $BF$ lines, with magnetic flux set by their average and electric charge equal to their difference. Representing level-$k$ torus states as normalized flux--charge wave packets, we prove that every fixed modular transformation of any fixed normalizable state with regular flux converges in the strong-$*$ topology to its $BF$ counterpart. The Dehn twist gives each line exactly its Aharonov--Bohm phase at every level, while $S$ converges to a Fourier transform exchanging flux and charge, without escaping to singular holonomies or large charges. States that approach singular fluxes at large $k$ are not covered. The natural boundary 2d theory is speculated to be a decompactified boson in the abelian case $G=U(1)$, and $\dim G$ non-compact free scalars for general $G$. For $SU(2)$, we discuss the gapped interfaces between adjacent levels, which must shift some flux or charge by a finite amount. In the $k\rightarrow\infty$ limit the interface is conjectured to be the $c=1$ Runkel--Watts theory.

title: A vertex operator algebra for the S-fold realisation of a non-unitary Haagerup--Izumi modular fusion category
summary: We show that there exists a strongly rational vertex operator algebra $V_{11}$, proposed by Flohr, whose representation theory $\mathrm{Rep}\,V_{11}\simeq\mathrm{Sem}\otimes\mathcal Z(σ_2\mathcal F)$ as braided categories. Here $\mathrm{Sem}$ is the semion category (with the spherical structure in which its generator has dimension $-1$), $\mathcal F$ is Ostrik's twisted Haagerup category and $σ_2$ is the Galois automorphism $ζ_{117}\mapstoζ_{117}^2$.

title: Quantum symmetric spaces at roots of 1
summary: We study the integral form of quantized coordinate algebras of symmetric spaces and its specializations at roots of unity. Our main tool is an integral localization, whose classical specialization recovers the open Borel orbit in the symmetric space. At a suitable odd root of unity, we prove that the quantum symmetric space is a finite projective module over its Frobenius center, which is canonically isomorphic to the classical coordinate algebra of the symmetric space. We show that the fibre algebras are isomorphic along each double Bruhat cell of the symmetric space. We determine the PI degree and propose a conjectural dimension formula for irreducible modules. In the simply connected case, we introduce a framed Kac-Moody data, which leads to a description of fibre algebras of quantum symmetric spaces via those of quantum Schubert cells.

title: Shifted quantum affine symmetric pairs: finite presentations and graded coideal structures
summary: Shifted quantum affine symmetric pair algebras were recently introduced as a trigonometric analogue of shifted twisted Yangians, whose truncations are expected to quantize fixed point loci in generalized affine Grassmannian slices. They are defined via a loop presentation with infinitely many generators and relations. In this paper, we consider anti-dominantly shifted quantum affine symmetric pair algebras of simply-laced split type. Our main result is a construction of a finite presentation à la Levendorskii. We apply it in type $\mathsf{A}$ to construct an embedding of a shifted quantum symmetric pair algebra into the corresponding shifted quantum affine algebra, yielding a graded coideal structure.

title: Biquandle Image Quivers
summary: We introduce a new family of weighted quiver-valued invariants of oriented classical and virtual knots and link, surface-knots and surface-links, and immersed surface-knots and surface-links associated to finite biquandles. We derive several polynomial invariants from these quivers via decategorification. We provide examples to illustrate the computation of the invariant as well as toy examples showing tables of invariant values for small biquandles.

title: The Anyon Atlas
summary: We classify possible topological quantum field theories in 2+1 dimensions with up to 22 anyons in the bosonic case and up to 26 in the fermionic case, through the modular data of modular and supermodular tensor categories. We construct such data via congruence representations of $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ using a numerical optimization algorithm that scales to high rank. We chart the relations between the resulting theories, including anyon condensations and Chern-Simons realizations. We find examples of modular data that do not appear to arise from any Chern-Simons theory by any sequence of condensations of anyons or gaugings of ordinary global symmetries. These examples give qualitatively new topological quantum field theories, which go beyond any notion of gauge theory. For examples in this class with 11 and 12 anyon types, we solve the pentagon and hexagon equations explicitly, showing that these modular data are realized by full unitary topological quantum field theories. We also introduce https://www.AnyonAtlas.org, an online resource for exploring the data.

title: Pre-Nichols algebras and generation of pointed Hopf algebras in positive characteristic
summary:
We study when a finite-dimensional pre-Nichols algebra $R$ of $V$ over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$, with $p\nmid\dim R$, is necessarily isomorphic to the Nichols algebra $\B(V)$. A trace identity gives a rigidity criterion involving the twist on minimal defining relations. Using integral forms and Hochschild cohomology, we establish uniform rigidity for Yetter--Drinfeld modules of bounded dimension over fixed finite abelian groups, and obtain related results for certain modules over nonabelian groups.
  For every finite group $G$ of odd order, outside finitely many characteristics depending only on $G$, every finite-dimensional pointed Hopf algebra $H$ with $G(H)\simeq G$ and dimension prime to the characteristic is generated by group-like and skew-primitive elements. If $G$ is abelian, then, outside a possibly larger finite set of characteristics, every such $H$ is a Hopf $2$-cocycle deformation of its associated graded Hopf algebra.

title: The center conjecture for cyclotomic Hecke algebras and cohomology of quiver varieties
summary:
For a quiver without edge loops, we construct an isomorphism from the cohomology of a Nakajima quiver variety with coefficients in an arbitrary field to the Jucys--Murphy center of the corresponding cyclotomic KLR algebra over that field. In affine type $A^{(1)}_{e-1}$, combining this with a dimension count shows that this Jucys--Murphy center coincides with the full center in characteristic $0$, when the characteristic does not divide $e$, and when the characteristic equals $e$. This follows from a geometric theorem showing that the sum of these cohomology rings is cocyclic as a module over an integral form of a loop algebra.
  As a consequence, we prove that the center of a cyclotomic Hecke algebra of type $G(r,1,n)$ with $q\neq 1$ over any field is generated by symmetric polynomials in its Jucys--Murphy elements, and the same holds over any commutative domain in which $q-1$ is invertible. We also prove a generalization to the integral case of the conjecture of Krylov, Paegelow and Shlykov identifying the equivariant $K$-theory of the core of a Gieseker variety with the cocenter of the generic cyclotomic Hecke algebra, including the natural extension of this conjecture to positive characteristic.

title: Classification of twisted Yangians as coideal subalgebras of Yangians
summary: Let $\mathfrak g$ be a complex simple Lie algebra with an involution $ω$. We classify the homogeneous right coideal subalgebras of the Yangian of $\mathfrak g$ whose classical limit is the enveloping algebra of the twisted current algebra, embedded in the standard way, without assuming any formula for the coaction. For nontrivial $ω$, they form a family parametrized by a spectral parameter and an element of the center of the fixed-point subalgebra; for $ω=\mathrm{id}$, only a spectral parameter occurs. All members of the family are isomorphic as graded algebras, through explicit isomorphisms. In particular, the twisted Yangians with a central correction introduced by Huang and Lu are coideal quantizations, and the $\imath$Yangian of quasi-split type $\mathsf A_{2n}$ is isomorphic to the traditional twisted Yangian studied by MacKay and by Belliard and Regelskis. The PBW property is proved uniformly from the classical affine Serre relations, without quantum defining relations. We also recover finite presentations in split and quasi-split types and verify the technical hypotheses of the quantum duality principle used by Lu, Wang, and Weekes.

title: Coactions of weak multiplier Hopf algebras
summary: In this article, we investigate the notion of a coaction for a weak multiplier Hopf algebra. We show that there is a duality for actions and coactions of weak algebraic quantum groups. Then we obtain the well known Blattner-Montgomery duality theorem for weak algebraic quantum groups in the framework of dual pairs. We form a Morita context when the weak multiplier Hopf algebra admits a two-sided faithful integral and show that the coaction is Galois if and only if the map in the Morita context is surjective. As an application, we obtain the result that a grading by any groupoid $G$ can be considered as a $\mathrm{C}G$-comodule algebra. We also construct a Morita context connecting the smash product $A\# \mathrm{C}(G)$ and the coinvariant subalgebra $A^{\mathrm{C}(G)}$. Finally we construct an isomorphism between $(R\# \mathrm{C}(G))\# \mathrm{C}G$ and $R\otimes (\mathrm{C}(G)\# \mathrm{C}G)$ when $R$ is graded by $G$.

title: Analytic quantum invariants
summary: Using a deformed Borel-Laplace resummation, we propose a framework for repackaging quantum invariants as analytic invariants. We illustrate our approach through a detailed analysis of the coloured Jones polynomials of several simple knots, deriving explicit expressions for the resulting analytic invariants in terms of $(q,X)$-series. These invariants are closely related to, but generally distinct from, those obtained via the conventional Borel resummation of the Melvin-Morton-Rozansky expansion. As a further example, we construct an analytic invariant from a sequence of two-variable polynomials conjectured to be the Links-Gould polynomials of the figure-eight knot, associated with the quantum superalgebras $U_q(\mathfrak{gl}(n|1))$. Finally, we apply our technique to $q$-series arising in the study of three-manifold invariants, revealing connections with mock modular forms.

title: A Hopf Algebraic Theory of the Quantum Magnusian
comment: 67 pages. The $e$ and $ω$ functions have been extended to arbitrary mixed graphs. The three-vertex contraction rule from the former Appendix A has been generalized to a $k$-vertex contraction rule for all $k\geq 2$ and moved to Section 6.4. The former Appendix B has also been incorporated into the main text, and both appendices have been removed
summary:
We develop a Hopf-algebraic theory of graph coefficients arising in the quantum Magnus expansion. At the classical level, the expansion is governed by directed trees, whereas its quantum counterpart involves loop graphs, multiple edges, and several types of edge data. We introduce a contraction Hopf algebra of mixed quivers containing these diagrams and closed under contraction.
  On this algebra we define a character $e$ from normalized linear-extension data, directed-tadpole factors, and a prescription for undirected edges, and let $ω$ be its convolution inverse. Our main result is a universal closed formula for the connected function $ω_c$ on every finite mixed quiver, expressed as a finite sum over ordered set partitions of the vertices. We also construct a weighted vertex-splitting Hopf structure on the unlocalized mixed-quiver algebra, with convolution $\star_V$ and canonical edge-weight character $ζ_V$, such that $ω_c=\log_{\star_V}ζ_V$. Compatibility of the two coproducts and an explicit identity between their characters explain this equality. We further prove that the two-vertex contraction identity, tadpole factorization, vanishing on disconnected graphs, and boundary data uniquely determine $ω_c$.
  For acyclic quivers, the formula reduces to a permutation formula with coefficients depending only on descent numbers. We derive this formula independently from the quantum Magnus expansion using operator products and Wick contractions, showing that the physical graph coefficients are governed by the convolution structure of the contraction Hopf algebra. Further consequences include a refined quantum Murua formula and orientation-sum identities related to Tutte and chromatic polynomials.

title: Iterative construction of the R-matrices in arbitrary dimensions
comment: 23 pages, no figures; added references in Sections 1 and 2
summary:
We investigate a special ansats that allows for an iterative solution of the constant Yang-Baxter equation. Testing this ansatz, we construct four sequences of the constant R-matrices. In each sequence the R-matrices act on the tensor squares of vector spaces of linearly growing dimensions. Each R-matrix also depends on a single complex parameter.
  By analyzing the spectra of the R-matrices, we conclude that the first and the third series are associated with the symmetric tensor representations of the quantum groups U_q(sl(2)) and U_q(sl(2|1)), respectively. The other two series appear to be related to representations of quantum groups in the case where q is a root of unity. The elements of the second series are associated with nilpotent representations of U_q(sl(2)).
  We also check the correspondence between these R-matrices and link invariants. Applying the Reshetikhin-Turaev procedure to the first, second, and fourth sequences yields, respectively, colored Jones polynomials, ADO invariants, and Alexander polynomials. To our surprise, a similar calculation for the third series yields a trivial result, identically equal to 1.

title: Langlands Duality and Invariant Differential Operators: the Case SL(2n+1)
summary: Recently we started building a bridge between two cases of Langlands duality. The latter is one of the most influential topics in mathematical research. It has many different appearances and influential subtopics. Yet there is a topic that until now seems unrelated to the Langlands program. That is the topic of invariant differential operators. That is strange since both items are deeply rooted in Harish-Chandra's representation theory of semisimple Lie groups. We started with the case of the group ~$SL(2n)$. In the present paper we deal with the group $SL(2n+1)$. The two mentioned groups are similar, but their representation theories is rather different.

title: Instanton slices and their superpolynomials
comment: v3: significant revision: stronger main connection conjecture, enhanced instanton formulas via nonsymmetric Macdonald polynomials, topological invariance of certain families of motivic superpolynomials, and some mixed characteristic conjecture, 106 pages; v4: Instanton Volume Conjecture added, more on superpolynomials of Gorenstein rings and multibranch ones, other improvements, 130 pages
summary:
The key theorem is a connection between motivic superpolynomials of plane curve singularities in any ranks with superpolynomials of the corresponding instanton slices, Nekrasov-type instanton sums with conductors. In this case, instanton slices are related to Compactified Jacobians, but they form a much wider class and, generally, have no connection to plane curve singularities. Thus, we extend significantly theory of affine Springer fibers in type A. For instance, we obtain a motivic interpretation (counting $\mathbb{F}_q$-points of some stacks) of superpolynomials for hyperbolic knots K12n242, K12n725, among many others. New formulas for Nekrasov's instanton sums as limits of superpolynomials of families of plane curve singularities are another application, with an impressive connection to nonsymmetric Macdonald polynomials.
  The main conjecture states that instanton superpolynomials for arbitrary Young diagrams coincide with the corresponding (new) DAHA superpolynomials if and only if the latter are positive or (equivalently) the former are superdual. Only very few such diagrams come from plane curve singularities. Our DAHA superpolynomials are parallel to the EHA ones, but we used the nonsymmetric approach. The connection with Khovanov-Rozansky polynomials of the corresponding Coxeter knots is expected. Among applications: the Volume Conjecture reformulated in terms of instanton slices, topological invariance of unibranch motivic superpolynomials for semigroups with up to 4 generators, a mixed-characteristic conjecture, upgraded Weak Riemann Hypothesis, and superpolynomials for Gorenstein curve singularities and multibranch ones.

title: GKLO representations for shifted quantum affine symmetric pairs
summary: In this note, we introduce shifted quantum affine symmetric pairs of split simply-laced type, and construct their GKLO representations, following similar recent developments in the case of shifted twisted Yangians. A full proof that our formulas yield a representation is given.

title: Covariant Bimodule Connections and Noncommutative Geometric Yang-Baxter Solutions
comment: Complete rewrite, including an extension from the quantum Grassmannians to all cominuscule quantum flag manifolds, and a proof that the bimodule map of our bimodule connection is a Yang--Baxter solution
summary: We introduce a new class of Yang--Baxter solutions, which we call \emph{noncommutative geometric solutions}, constructed from quantum group noncommutative geometries. These solutions are built from a quantum homogeneous space, endowed with a covariant differential graded algebra and a noncommutative Koszul connection $\nabla$. If $\nabla$ is a bimodule connection, that is, if its generalised flip map $σ$ is well defined, then a simple set of sufficient conditions for $σ$ to be a Yang--Baxter solution is given. These results are applied to the cominuscule quantum flag manifolds $\mathcal{O}_q(G/L_S)$ endowed with their Heckenberger--Kolb calculi. The noncommutative complex geometry of the calculi decomposes their Yang--Baxter operator $σ$ into three parts: holomorphic, anti-holomorphic, and cross-type. For the non-exceptional examples, the holomorphic and anti-holomorphic solutions recover, up to scalar multiple, the usual quasitriangular braidings of the associated Drinfeld--Jimbo $U_q(\mathfrak{l}_S^s)$-modules. However, we get a new extension of these braidings to the direct sum, which remarkably restricts to an involutive operator on the cross terms. As an application, we produce a simple uniform presentation of the degree two relations of the Heckenberger--Kolb calculi as a \emph{quantum exterior algebra} associated to the generalised flip map $σ$.

title: Reconstruction of tensor categories of type $G_2$
summary: We prove that any ribbon tensor category $\mathcal{C}$ with the fusion rules of the compact group of type $G_2$ is equivalent to the representation category of the corresponding Drinfeld-Jimbo quantum group for $q^2=1$ or $q^2$ not a root of unity. We also prove an analogous result for the corresponding ribbon fusion tensor categories at roots of unity.

title: Derived derivations govern contraderived deformations of dg algebras over dg (pr)operads
comment: 18pp, two independent proofs; v2 minor changes
summary: We show that Hinich's simplicial nerve of the differential graded Lie algebra (DGLA) of derived derivations of a dg algebra $A$ over a dg properad $\mathcal{P}$ is equivalent to the space of deformations of $A$ as a $\mathcal{P}_{\infty}$-algebra in Positselski's contraderived dg category. This resolves Hinich's counterexamples to the general existence of derived deformations. It also generalises his results when $A$ is homologically bounded below, since contraderived deformations are then precisely derived deformations.

title: On a specialization of Toda eigenfunctions
summary: This paper studies rational functions $\mathfrak{J}_α(q)$, which depend on a positive element $α$ of the root lattice of a root system. These functions arise as Shapovalov pairings of Whittaker vectors in Verma modules of highest weight $-ρ$ for quantum groups and as Hilbert series of Zastava spaces, and are related to the Toda system. They are specializations of multivariate functions more commonly studied in the literature. We investigate the denominator of these rational functions and give an explicit combinatorial formula for the numerator in type A. We also propose a conjectural realization of the numerator as the Poincaré polynomial of a smooth variety in type A.

title: Affine highest weight structures on module categories over quiver Hecke algebras
summary: We prove that the category of finitely generated graded modules over the quiver Hecke algebra of arbitrary type admits numerous stratifications in the sense of Kleshchev. A direct consequence is that the full subcategory corresponding to the quantum unipotent subgroup associated with any Weyl group element is an affine highest weight category. Our results significantly generalize earlier works by Kato, Brundan, Kleshchev, McNamara and Muth. The key ingredient is a realization of standard modules via determinantial modules. We utilize the technique of R-matrices to study these standard modules.

title: From vertex operator superalgebras to graded-local conformal nets and back
summary: We generalize the Carpi-Kawahigashi-Longo-Weiner correspondence between vertex operator algebras and conformal nets to the case of vertex operator superalgebras and graded-local conformal nets by introducing the notion of strongly graded-local vertex operator superalgebra. Then we apply our machinery to a number of well-known examples including superconformal field theory models. We also prove that all lattice VOSAs are strongly graded-local. Furthermore, we prove strong graded-locality of the super-Moonshine VOSA, whose group of automorphisms preserving the superconformal structure is isomorphic to Conway's largest sporadic simple group, and of the shorter Moonshine VOSA, whose automorphisms group is isomorphic to the direct product of the baby Monster with a cyclic group of order two.
